correctness.rationale: Verified the full scope n>=3, every permutation of n once-only Rule 150 updates repeated on a binary cycle. Each update swaps edge differences y_{i-1},y_i; the even-parity edge vector has two vertex anchors. Source/sink conjugations reduce any schedule with k cyclic ascents to two edge rotations of lengths k and m=n-k. Requiring their t-power return and zero anchor cocycle imposes two parity constraints on gcd(k,t)+gcd(m,t) periodic edge-pattern bits. The constraint determinant is n*t/(g*h) mod 2, giving rank 1+epsilon, hence exactly 2^(g+h-epsilon) complete fixed states including both anchor choices. Faithful permutation action on even-parity edge words and the terminal anchor parity prove the stated lcm/twice-lcm order; Eulerian cyclic-ascent counting gives n*A(n-1,k-1). I separately implemented direct vertex scan, bitmatrix nullities, predicted orders, and brute orbit checks for all 870 scan permutations n=3..6 (50,352 state evaluations); all matched. The finite checks corroborate, do not prove the arbitrary-n result.
